context.description: A spend cap stops the task for a human before any nudge

evidence.trustReason: Given a building task: the test folds the stored slice through a real Recorder and asserts unitState(T1.1)=building, the T1.1:building tag and the builder session before it spawns the real TaskSupervisor machine. When a retry status names the spend cap: test 1 publishes a real SessionStatus retry event on the real bus; the real sessionEvents relay and the spendCap guard act. When the turn's error names the spend cap: test 2 ends the turn with an assistant error message that the real spendCapError reads. Then task.needs_human with a 'spend cap:' reason: both tests assert the stored fact equals task.needs_human for T1.1 with reason 'spend cap: <message>' and startsWith('spend cap:'), and the run actor folds T1.1 to needs_human; test 1 also asserts the turn was cancelled. And no nudge: both assert the stored types equal exactly ['task.needs_human'], context.nudges is 0 and only one prompt went out. Controls prove the assertions can fail: a non-cap retry records nothing, and a non-cap turn error records task.nudged 1. Only the model boundary is scripted. Fresh run: 2 pass, 0 fail, 26 expect calls.
